result.rationale: The diff confirms the finding: in zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is called with 'credentialId' as the third argument while every other call site (googlecalendar, hubspot, lark, office365, webex, zohocrm, zoom) passes 'credential.userId'. refreshOAuthTokens sends this value as 'calcomUserId' to the sync endpoint, and the webhook handler looks up prisma.user by reqBody.userId — passing a credential id would either fail to match a user or match the wrong user, causing credentials to be written to the wrong user. judged_text: zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-93) passes credentialId — the credential's primary key — where every other call site passes credential.userId, so refreshOAuthTokens sends the wrong id as calcomUserId: sync fails, or worse, the webhook handler (app-credential.ts:34,62-65) matches some other user's id and writes this user's tokens onto another user's credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `refreshOAuthTokens` the third parameter is explicitly treated as a Cal.com *userId* (it checks `userId` truthiness and sends it as `calcomUserId` in the POST body). Nearly all call sites in this diff pass `credential.userId`, but `zoho-bigin` passes `credentialId` instead (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which is inconsistent and (by name/usage) likely the credential primary key rather than the user id. If `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is enabled, this will send the wrong identifier and break credential sync (or cause the external endpoint to act on the wrong user). The finding’s additional claim about the webhook handler overwriting another user’s credential isn’t directly shown, but the wrong-id bug in the sync request is verifiable from the diff.
